# Energy / XLE — 2026-09-25

This is the **mirror-image of yesterday**. On 09-24 the barrel was green, XLE was the board's top premarket sector (+1.11%), and the driver was a fresh US–Iran kinetic escalation — the book flipped to up/mild and hit. This morning **the rotation has reversed**: XLE is **−0.99% premarket**, the **only red sector on the board** (XLK +0.79%, XLU +0.30%, XLF +0.09%), while the barrel is **offered** and the broad tape is **mildly green** (ES +0.28%, NQ +0.57%). That is the 09-21 configuration — *sector is the clear laggard on a green tape* — not the 09-23 configuration (sector leading a flat board). The trap today is carrying yesterday's up/mild into a session where the sector's own object is red and the sector is the board's worst print.

## Channel 2

**1. Shared macro as it hits energy.** The tape is **mildly risk-on, tech-led, and energy is the funding source**: ES=F **+0.28%**, NQ=F **+0.57%**; Finviz ES/NQ/RTY/DJIA **+0.20% / +0.41% / +0.08% / +0.11%** agree in sign. Asia composite **−0.06%** (Nikkei +1.3%, Kospi +1.04%, Hang Seng −1.01%, Shanghai −1.22%, ASX −0.43%), Europe **+0.64%** (DAX +0.85%, EuroStoxx +0.88%, FTSE +0.5%). **VIX 15.38 (−0.29 1d) with VIX/VIX3M 0.835 — contango**, so the 09-14 full-weight de-risking debit is **off**. **USD is a non-event** (DXY −0.2% 1d, Finviz USD −0.02%) — no commodity headwind, marginally a tailwind. **Real yields rising** (DFII10 **2.76, +0.13 1d / +0.38 1m**; DGS10 **5.11, +0.15 1d / +0.41 1m**; DGS30 5.4) — secondary vs oil, but a genuine multiple headwind, and the 5-day 10Y-SPX corr is **−0.958**, so duration is the dominant SPX transmission. News Judge #1–#4 (10Y tops 5.2%, Williams "another hike reasonable," Warsh JH hike-odds, mortgage surge) is the **dominant macro cluster** and it is **bearish SPX beta / hawkish rates** — but the tape is *green*, so the hawkish cluster is not the live impulse for equities this morning; it is a cap on extension, not a sign-setter. Critically, **energy is NOT the rotation destination today**: the green tape is funding XLK (+0.79%) and XLU (+0.30%), and XLE is the **only red sector**. Per 09-21, when the sector ETF is the clear laggard on a green tape, the green tape is the **funding mechanism for rotation OUT of the laggard** — score S0 negative. **S0 = −0.5** (not −1: the tape is only mildly green, not ≥ +1%, and there is no USD headwind; but the laggard-on-green-tape precondition is met).

**2. Spine (S1).** One cluster: live offered barrel **plus** geo-premium fade **plus** the 09-23 EIA build. Count it **once**.
- **Crude: offered, live-verified.** Channel 1 CL=F **−1.71%** 1d, BZ=F **−7.41%** 1d. The Brent −7.41% is a **contract-roll / expiry distortion** (same class of artifact as 09-22's CL=F −4.78% and 09-23's CL=F −4.97%), so it is **rejected as the live increment**; the WTI −1.71% is the more credible live read. Finviz WTI $104.16 / Brent $107.67 is the **stale 09-16 column** and is rejected outright. Live independent quotes (Channel 2 search) put WTI in the **~$90–93** area and Brent **~$99–102**, i.e. a **sub-2% offered** barrel, not a collapse. Sign **DOWN**, increment **sub-2%**.
- **Geo premium still physically tight, not transmitting — fading.** The 09-24 US–Iran kinetic headlines (Saudi/Houthi strikes, Trump "hopefully nearing end of Iran war") are **already in yesterday's tape**; this morning there is **no fresh kinetic increment** (News Judge: no fresh kinetic/oil increment). Hormuz visible traffic remains a handful of ships vs pre-war 85–125. Oil is **falling**, so this is fade/non-confirmation. **Do not** score Crude oil price surge. **Do not** score a fresh Geopolitical supply risk premium HIT. 09-15's physical-increment license is **off**.
- **Inventory: EIA build is the live print, already in the tape.** WPSR week ending 9/18 printed **09-23**: crude **+2.969 Mb** (per the 09-24 reflect), against a WSJ survey expectation of **−0.5 Mb** — a **relative build miss**. API (week ending 9/18) had already leaned build: crude **+1.786 Mb**, Cushing **+2.082 Mb**, gasoline −2.16 Mb, distillates −2.16 Mb. This is a **live Inventory build** HIT — but it is **already in 09-23's −1.09% and 09-24's tape**, so it is counted **inside** the oil-down cluster, not as a second spine. Do not date it as a fresh 09-25 print.
- **OPEC+ (carried offset):** Sep **+188 kb/d** completed the 2023 voluntary-cut rollback; **6 Sep** meeting **held October unchanged**. Next core-group meeting **Oct 4**. Not a cut, not a quota break.
- **Demand destruction (carried official):** hawkish Fed/SEP + Williams "another hike reasonable" is a medium-horizon demand lid, not a 1d EIA-style HIT. IEA vs OPEC disagreement is leftover.
- **Cracks:** MAP HEAT **Refining dir=up** (MPC:pos, VLO:pos) — but this is a **nested refiner-sleeve** signal, and today HO **+0.18%** / RBOB **−0.54%** / gasoil **−0.26%** are **not** a clean squeeze. Dampen; do not let VLO/MPC set the ETF.
- **Nat gas $2.902 (−0.51%)** — no surge; N/A for oil-weighted XLE.
- **MAP HEAT nested:** **OVERRIDE** Oil & Gas Drilling **down** (breadth 0.0, price rejecting contract news); **OVERRIDE** Oil & Gas Equipment & Services **down, high conviction** (breadth 0.021, w1 −6.75%, every captain red); **OVERRIDE** Thermal Coal **down** (breadth 0.0); **OVERRIDE** Uranium **down, high conviction** (breadth 0.077, w1 −9.4%, both captains down double digits). **HEAT** E&P up (medium), Integrated up (medium, refining-margin proxy), Midstream flat (low). The nested **overrides are four-of-six subsectors down**, and per the sector layer they **do not average into the parent ETF** — but they confirm the tape's message that the complex is being sold, not bought.

Net **S1 = −1**. Live oil sign is down once, with the EIA build and geo-fade counted inside the same cluster. Not −2: the increment is sub-2%, not a collapse, and the nested E&P/Integrated/Refining HEATs are a partial offset. Not 0: the barrel is genuinely offered and the sector is the board laggard.

**3. Breadth.** Channel 1 tape: XLE 1d rel **+0.45%** (yesterday's mild outperformance — leftover, not live), 3d rel **+1.04%**, 1w rel **−3.19%**, 1m rel **+1.06%**. The **live** signal is the premarket board: **XLE −0.99%** is the **only red sector** vs XLK +0.79%, XLU +0.30%, XLF +0.09%, XLV −0.01%, XLP −0.12%, XLI −0.38%. That is a genuine same-morning breadth **failure** into energy on a green tape — the mirror of 09-14's "only green sector" (which the 09-14 reflect correctly flagged as *not* breadth). Here the ETF's own red print is the laggard signal, and the nested MAP HEAT overrides (Drilling/Services/Coal/Uranium all down, breadth 0.0–0.077) confirm **intra-sector constituent participation is negative**, not just the ETF. **S2 = −1.**

**4. Flows / positioning.** XLE still carries the multi-week outflow hangover. 1m rel **+1.06%** is **not** crowded (≪ +8%), so the 09-10 crowded-long unwind trigger does **not** fire — this is not a positioning-driven fade, it is a factor-driven one. 1w rel **−3.19%** shows the sector has been bleeding relative for a week. No index rebalance / inclusion event. **S3 = 0** (no crowding debit, no forced-flow signal; the outflow hangover is a washout-setup positive later, not a same-day demand signal).

**5. Earnings / policy catalysts.** No XLE-relevant earnings today. News Judge #1–#4 are the hawkish-rates cluster (bearish SPX beta, a cap on energy's multiple, not a sign-setter for the sector's own object). News Judge #5–#8 (ASML EUV sold out, APH −6.5%, Bloom Energy/Oracle, Ciena upgrade) are **AI-infra / tech**, not energy. **Checked, nothing material** for energy specifically beyond the rates cluster already scored in S0.

**6. ETF tape (S4).** Channel 1 relative returns are **prior-close** data (through 09-24): 1d rel +0.45%, 3d rel +1.04%. Per the 09-17 leftover-S4 gate, these are **not** live confirmation. The **live** tape is PM:XLE **−0.99%** — which is *extension of the down move*, not a flat print. So S4 is scored as **confirmation of the down lean**, but only at −1 (the prior-close series is mildly positive, so the tape is not unanimously red). **S4 = −1.**

**Divergence check.** Leading factor sum (S0 −0.5, S1 −1, S2 −1, S3 0) = **−2.5**, and S4 = −1 confirms. **No divergence** — factors and tape agree on the down lean. This is the opposite of 09-23 (where the tape diverged bullish and the card wrongly resolved against it); here the tape diverges **bearish** and the factors agree, so the resolution is straightforward.

**Magnitude discipline.** Energy mag hit-rate last-30 is **0.37** (< 0.4), oil increment is **sub-2%** (not >5%), and XLE PM is **−0.99%** (not >2% in either direction). Per 09-08/09-09 and the 09-18 band refinement, **cap at mild**. The 09-21 notable-lift precondition (PM ≤ −1% AND barrel offered AND tape risk-on) is **partially** met (PM −0.99% is essentially at the −1% line, barrel offered, tape mildly green) — but the tape is only **+0.28%/+0.57%**, not the ≥ +1% risk-on funding squeeze of 09-21, and the oil increment is sub-2%, not the ~2%+ of 09-21. So the notable lift does **not** fire; **mild** is the correct band. Direction **down**.

**Confidence.** Direction signals are aligned (S0, S1, S2, S4 all negative; no divergence), but the magnitude hit-rate is low and the increment is modest. Confidence **0.52** — keep direction, shrink confidence on modest |score| per the open sector_energy DO-INSTEAD.

# Sector Post-Session Review — Energy / XLE — 2026-09-25

## 0. FACTS

**Path:** Open $61.92 (already below prior close), close $62.04. The ETF did **not** gap-and-fade from a green open; it opened red and stayed red, with a modest intraday bid into the close. No reversal of sign at any point in the deterministic open/close pair.

## 1. What drove the sector

**Taxonomy mapping (what actually fired):**
- **Crude price collapse / oil offered** — the live spine. The card scored this as "sub-2% offered" and it printed ~2% down. **HIT.**
- **Geopolitical supply risk premium** — **faded**, not paid. Truce hopes overrode fresh Saudi attacks. **MISS** (correctly scored MISS in the grid).
- **Sector rotation out of energy** — the green tape funded XLK/XLU while XLE was the only red sector. **HIT.**
- **Sector breadth failure** — nested subsector overrides (Drilling/Services/Coal/Uranium down) confirmed. **HIT.**
- **Real yields rising** — DFII10 +0.13 1d, DGS10 +0.15 1d; a genuine multiple headwind on a rate-sensitive real-asset complex. **HIT.**
- **USD weakening** — DXY −0.2%; a marginal tailwind that did **not** save the sector. **HIT** as a fact, but it was a non-factor in the outcome.

## 2. Audit of morning S0–S4 reads against reality

**S0_SHARED_MACRO = −0.5 — VERDICT: CORRECT, arguably under-scored.**
The card's core S0 logic was the 09-21 configuration: *sector ETF is the clear laggard on a green tape → the green tape is the funding mechanism for rotation OUT of the laggard.* That is exactly what happened. XLE −0.89% vs SPY +0.54% is a textbook laggard-on-green-tape print. The card's decision to score S0 negative rather than zero — and to explicitly reject the "residual geo/cracks floor" cap — was the right call and is the single most important correct read of the session. If anything, −0.5 was conservative: the relative underperformance (−1.44%) was larger than the −0.99% premarket print implied, and the rotation-out was unambiguous. But the card's stated reason for not going to −1 (tape only mildly green, no USD headwind) was defensible at the open. **Keep the sign; the magnitude was slightly light.**

**S1_SECTOR_FACTORS = −1 — VERDICT: CORRECT.**
The card counted the oil-down cluster **once** (live offered barrel + geo-premium fade + EIA build), refused to double-count the EIA build as a second spine, and refused to score a fresh geopolitical premium HIT. All three refusals were correct:

## 3. Interactions / double-count / knowable-at-open test

**Double-count audit:** The card's central discipline was counting the oil-down cluster **once**. Three candidate spines were collapsed into one:
1. Live offered barrel (WTI −1.71%)
2. Geo-premium fade (truce hopes)
3. EIA build (crude +2.969 Mb, printed 09-23)

All three are the **same underlying move** (oil down on de-escalation + loose inventories). Counting them separately would have produced S1 ≈ −3 and likely a notable band. The card's refusal to do so was the difference between a correct mild call and a likely magnitude miss. **No double-count occurred.**

**The one interaction the card under-weighted:** The card treated the geo-fade as "non-confirmation" and the EIA build as "already in the tape," which is correct for *scoring*, but it slightly under-stated that the **truce headline was a fresh, same-morning catalyst** (published 01:11 GMT). The card said "no fresh kinetic increment" — true for *kinetic* (escalation) headlines, but there **was** a fresh *de-escalation* headline, and that was the live impulse. The card's S1 sign was right; its characterization of the catalyst as "fade/non-confirmation" rather than "active de-escalation driver" was a framing miss, not a scoring miss.

**Knowable-at-open test:** **YES.** Every material input was available pre-open:
- Truce-hopes headline: 01:11 GMT (pre-US-open)
- WTI −1.71% / Brent artifact: pre-open
- EIA build: printed 09-23, two days prior
- XLE PM −0.99%, only red sector: pre-open
- ES +0.28% / NQ +0.57% green tape: pre-open
- Real yields rising (DFII10 +0.13): pre-open

There is **no post-open information** that changed the sign or the band. This was a fully knowable-at-open down/mild call. The card's only self-inflicted friction was the Brent −7.41% artifact, which it correctly rejected — but the fact that it had to spend analytical budget rejecting a stale/rolled print is a process cost, not an outcome cost.

**Interaction the card got right that is easy to miss:** The card explicitly noted that the hawkish-rates cluster (News Judge #1–#4: 10Y tops 5.2%, Williams "another hike reasonable") was **bearish SPX beta but not the live impulse** because the tape was green. That is correct — the green tape meant rates were a *cap on extension*, not a *sign-setter*. Had the card scored the hawkish cluster as a live negative for energy, it would have over-scored S0. It didn't. Good discipline.

## 5. Verdict and lessons

**Direction: HIT.** Down called, down printed.
**Magnitude: HIT.** Mild called, mild printed (−0.89% ETF, −1.44% rel).
**All four scored components: correct sign.** S0 −0.5, S1 −1, S2 −1, S3 0, S4 −1 — every one matched reality.
**Divergence: correctly identified as absent.**
**Knowable-at-open: yes.**

This was a **clean, well-executed call** — the mirror-image framing of 09-24 was structurally correct, the laggard-on-green-tape rule (09-21) fired and resolved correctly, the double-count discipline held, and the magnitude cap held. The card avoided the 09-23 error (resolving against a divergent tape) precisely because there was no divergence to mis-resolve.

**Two process notes for the lesson file:**

1. **The "no fresh kinetic increment" framing was too narrow.** The card looked for fresh *escalation* headlines and, finding none, treated the geo premium as passively fading. In fact there was a fresh *de-escalation* headline (US–Iran truce hopes, 01:11 GMT) that was the active driver. **Lesson: when auditing a geo premium, search for both escalation AND de-escalation headlines; a truce headline is a fresh increment in the opposite direction, not a non-event.** The sign was right anyway, but the framing could have caused a miss in a different configuration (e.g., if the card had used "no fresh kinetic increment" to justify a *smaller* S1 than warranted).

2. **The DO-INSTEAD confidence shrink was applied even though magnitude did not miss.** The card shrank confidence to 0.52 on a fully-aligned call. The DO-INSTEAD says "shrink confidence on modest |score| when magnitude historically misses" — the conditional is "when magnitude historically misses," and today it didn't. **Lesson: the confidence shrink should be conditional on the magnitude hit-rate being the binding constraint, not applied reflexively to every modest-|score| call.** A fully-aligned, no-divergence, knowable-at-open call deserves confidence closer to 0.6–0.65 even at modest |score|.

3. **The Brent −7.41% artifact rejection was the highest-value single decision of the session.** It prevented an over-score that would likely have pushed the band to notable and produced a magnitude miss. **Lesson: contract-roll/expiry artifacts in the front-month series are a recurring trap (09-22 CL −4.78%, 09-23 CL −4.97%, 09-25 BZ −7.41%); the WTI front-month read is the more credible live increment when the two diverge by >3 points.** This rule is now three-for-three and should be promoted from a per-session note to a standing sector_energy rule.

**Net:** A correct down/mild call, cleanly executed, with the only deductions being (a) a slightly narrow catalyst framing and (b) a slightly over-conservative confidence. The sector's relative underperformance (−1.44%) was larger than the premarket print implied, so if anything the card left a little magnitude on the table — but mild was the right band and the notable-lift refusal was correct.
